disposition_reason: 381-page Expert Committee final report with three technical attachments. It contains substantial original occurrence data (SD industry tables for beans, peeled beans, nibs, shells, liquor, powder, butter and chocolate by origin/producing country/year; AYS retail chocolate percentiles by cacao group and organic/single-origin status; Expert Committee Ecuador bean sampling) plus measured process-control data (factory bean cleaning and winnowing study, on-farm fermentation/drying Pb) and Prop 65 consent-judgment triggers.
disposition_locator: Attachment 1 Appendix A Tables 3a-24, Appendix D Tables D-1/D-2; Attachment 2 Tables 5-6, Appendix C Tables C-1 to C-5; Attachment 3 Tables 3-15; Final Report Tables 3-4

study.design: expert committee report under a Prop 65 consent judgment, compiling (a) blinded Settling Defendant industry testing data (Batches 1-3), (b) As You Sow market testing of chocolate products, (c) Expert Committee field sampling in Ecuador, (d) a factory bean cleaning/winnowing study, and (e) literature review
study.material_scope: whole cocoa beans, peeled beans/grains, separated nibs and shells, cocoa liquor, cocoa powder, cocoa butter, chocolate by cacao % (SD data); retail chocolate products incl. cocoa powder/nibs in >95% group (AYS); process streams (factory)
study.growing_origin_vs_market: SD tables give either country of bean ORIGIN or PRODUCING (processing) country - kept separate. AYS data: products purchased in California, bean origin not given (single-origin flag only). Factory study: Ivory Coast beans processed in North America. Field sampling: Ecuador (Guayaquil area).
study.collection_period: SD Batch 1 chocolate tables: 2015-2018; Batch 3 nibs/shells: 2016-2018; other SD batches: not reported (data received Mar-Jun 2019). AYS products: 2014-2020. Ecuador sampling: 18 Nov 2019. Factory study: 17-19 Aug 2020.
study.sampling_unit: SD: individual industry test results (blinded, lot/sample level unknown); AYS: retail products (~587); Ecuador: composite of 3 pods per tree (3 trees) and market grab samples (12); factory: composites/individual stream samples per replicate
study.method: SD: 'ICP Mass Spec' (12 samples GFAAS), no further details; AYS: commercial labs, method by product record; Ecuador and factory: ICP-MS (EPA 6020A, ALS; Eurofins)
study.lod_loq: SD: not provided (values with '<' treated as LOD); Batch 3 Pb LOD 1.7 ppb (table key); Ecuador Pb MDL 3 ppb, reporting limit 19-20 ppb; AYS LODs obtained but not printed; factory LOD not stated
study.basis: mostly not stated (as received/as sold); Ecuador tree beans oven-dried (dry weight); literature values dry weight where stated
study.qa: SD: no QA/QC information; Expert Committee flagged possible Whirl-Pak bag contamination. Factory/Ecuador: not reported beyond lab method.

controls.control: Mechanical bean cleaning (screening, aspiration, destoning, magnet) before roasting/breaking
controls.design: factory process sampling (5 production replicates, one 100 t Ivory Coast lot)
controls.comparator: received (uncleaned) whole beans vs mechanically cleaned beans
controls.outcome: whole-bean Pb mean 95.2 ppb (n=12, highest 370) -> 39.7 ppb (n=6, highest 64) (-58%); variance 11,500 -> 166 ppb^2; one-sided t-test significant. Removed streams: 'unders' <2.0 mm 3,130 ppb (0.3% of mass), aspiration dust 2,370 ppb (0.1%), overs 44.5 ppb (0.1%).
controls.locator: Attachment 2 Appendix C Tables C-1, C-5; Table 5 p. 73; Executive summary s.4.2

controls.control: Wet washing of beans with detergent, and detergent followed by acid
controls.comparator: received beans (95.2 ppb, n=12) vs detergent (0.1% sodium lauryl sulfate) vs detergent + 1.0 M nitric acid; also vs mechanical cleaning (39.7)
controls.outcome: detergent 42.3 ppb (variance 81.1; n=6; not different from mechanical); detergent + acid 23.2 ppb (variance 13.4; n=6; -76% vs received, significantly lower than mechanical and detergent). Committee rated chemical washing 'Low' confidence because of Salmonella/mycotoxin/flavour risks of wet processing. Protocol named 1.0 M HCl; results name nitric acid.
controls.locator: Attachment 2 Table 6 p. 76; Table 7; Appendix C Table C-5 p. C-6

controls.control: Bean breaking/winnowing set-up favouring larger nib particles; do not route winnower fines into nib stream
controls.comparator: nib fractions by winnower screen size (6.00 mm to <1.00 mm)
controls.outcome: nib Pb: prewinnower 6.00 mm 28.9 ppb; channel 1 (5.16 mm) 19.9; ch2 (4.04) 15.2; ch3 (3.04) 32.0; ch4 (2.24) 41.7; ch5 (1.00) 77.7; ch6 fines (<1.00 mm) 143.0 ppb (2.4% of nib flow). Al (soil proxy) 25.7 -> 132.4 ppm with decreasing size. Non-parametric trend test significant. Overall nib 31.8 ppb; shell-in-nib (1.63% x 363 ppb shell) contributes ~6.3 ppb; fines (2.4% x 143) ~3.4 ppb; ~22.1 ppb (~70%) attributed to contact during bean breaking/winnowing.
controls.locator: Attachment 2 Appendix C Tables C-2, C-3, C-4 pp. C-3 to C-4

controls.control: Establish bean cleaning/winnowing QA practices for Pb (SOPs, preventive maintenance, calibration, SIN testing, routine liquor Pb testing)
controls.comparator: current industry practice (bean cleaning run for foreign matter, not Pb)
controls.outcome: Rated High confidence (confidence 69%, feasibility 78%, overall 76%); experts split on magnitude (unknown x2, >25%, <10%). Ahn: liquor Pb ~0.094 ppm feasible with existing cleaning; Brazil and Indonesia liquor/powder Pb higher than other processing countries despite non-elevated bean Pb, attributed to less effective cleaning.
controls.locator: Attachment 2 s.5.1.2 pp. 70-73, Table 4; Attachment 3 s.3.1 p. 9

controls.control: Prevent soil/dust contact of wet beans during fermentation and drying (raised tables, tarps, clean surfaces; avoid roadside/ground drying)
controls.design: on-farm sampling (Trinidad, two farms) and Expert Committee Ecuador market sampling
controls.comparator: Farm 1 vs Farm 2 during fermentation/drying (Ramtahal unpublished); beans picked up from ground vs beans kept in canvas bags (Ecuador market)
controls.outcome: Farm 1 shell Pb 200 (day 0) -> 2,400/4,200/2,700 -> 2,500 ppb final; nib <4 -> 14/35/18 -> 17 ppb. Farm 2 shell 68 -> 71 ppb; nib <4 ppb throughout. Ecuador market: beans from ground (Market 4) Pb 216-251 ppb, Al 419,000-704,000 µg/kg vs beans in canvas bags not touching ground (Market 5) Pb 7-14 ppb (J), Al 12,700-17,900 µg/kg. Pre-harvest Ecuador tree beans Pb 4-15 ppb (J). Strategy rated High confidence (75% confidence, 71% feasibility).
controls.locator: Attachment 1 Table 24 p. A-26; Appendix D Tables D-1/D-2; Attachment 2 s.4.4.1.1

controls.control: Point-of-purchase screening of bean lots for soil contamination (e.g., ferrozine Fe colour test) and rejection/rewashing of dirty beans
controls.comparator: no screening; handheld XRF found too insensitive
controls.outcome: Proposed by Chaney; no measured outcome. 'Test surfaces of cocoa beans for Pb at point of purchase' rated High confidence (63% confidence, 57% feasibility).
controls.locator: Final Report s.3.2 p. 7; Attachment 3 s.3.2 pp. 10-11; Attachment 2 s.6.1.3

controls.control: Blend high-Cd beans or liquor with low-Cd (e.g., West African) material
controls.outcome: Expected 10-25% or greater Cd reduction for non-single-origin products; no published data; rated High confidence (75% confidence, 79% feasibility). Ahn: ~60% of LAC (Ecuador/Peru/Venezuela) liquor exceeds current Consent Judgment Cd triggers and ~70% the drop-down triggers, limiting blending for fine-flavour products. SD figure note: US-produced liquor median Cd 600 ppb with Ecuadorian beans vs 68.3 ppb without.
controls.locator: Attachment 2 s.5.1.1 pp. 67-69; Final Report s.3.1 pp. 5-6; Attachment 3 s.4.1; Attachment 1 Fig. 7 note

controls.control: Source from low-Cd growing regions; exporters stop buying beans from high Cd-phytoavailability regions; avoid new orchards there
controls.design: SD industry testing (Batch 1 whole beans, by country of origin)
controls.outcome: Whole-bean Cd medians (ppb): Ivory Coast 60 (n=166), Nigeria 55, Ghana 70, Sao Tome 78, Cameroon 90, Brazil 94 vs Ecuador 511 (n=1,097), Peru 542, Venezuela 892, Colombia 2,865, Trinidad 410.5. Ahn: LAC beans ~10x West African Cd; CODEX cocoa powder data LAC 8.7x Africa. Strategies rated High confidence (94% and 81%).
controls.locator: Attachment 1 Table 3a p. A-2; Attachment 3 s.4.1 p. 30; Attachment 2 s.4.1.1-4.1.2

controls.control: Choose conventional/blended over organic and/or single-origin chocolate (product category signal)
controls.comparator: conventional blended vs organic and/or single-origin products, by cacao group
controls.outcome: Cd medians (ppm): Group 1 0.040 vs 0.180; Group 2 0.064 vs 0.220; Group 3 0.290 vs 0.565 (p<0.001 for means). Status-quo compliance with 0.120/0.175/0.400 ppm Cd: bulk 84/83/67% vs specialty 26/34/25%. Pb not significantly different (e.g., Group 2 median 0.028 vs 0.027 ppm), except Group 3 single-origin Pb lower than blended (p<0.05).

controls.control: Raise soil pH by liming (hydrated lime, limestone, dolomite)
controls.outcome: Ramtahal et al. 2019 (Trinidad): 4.5 and 6 t Ca(OH)2/ha reduced LEAF Cd 37% and 20% at 3 months (effect to 9 months). Arguello 2019 greenhouse: 4 t/ha limestone reduced leaf Cd 1.7-fold. Davila 2018 (Peru, via CODEX; not verifiable): dolomite 1.81/2.72/3.63 t/ha reduced bean Cd by 0.52/0.47/0.45 ppm. Surface liming in orchards acts slowly; one test showed reduced uptake from top layer but increased uptake from deeper soil. Rated High confidence (75%). Secondary citation reported in the AYS report; Expert Committee could not verify the cited primary in several cases.
controls.locator: Attachment 2 s.4.1.3 pp. ~20-23; Attachment 3 s.4.2 p. 33

controls.control: Zinc sulfate soil amendment (Zn competes with Cd on ZIP transporter)
controls.outcome: SENESCYT 2011 (Ecuador, via CODEX; not verifiable): 200 kg Zn/ha reduced SOIL Cd 1.35 -> 0.59 mg/kg (-56%); no tissue data. Davila 2018: modest bean Cd reduction at 0.09-0.27 kg ZnSO4/plant (details unavailable). dos Santos 2020 greenhouse CCN-51 seedlings: 26-105 mg Zn/kg strongly inhibited root/leaf Cd at 22 mg/kg added Cd. Foliar Zn judged ineffective (Low confidence 19%). Soil ZnSO4 rated High (69%). Secondary citation reported in the AYS report; Expert Committee could not verify the cited primary in several cases.

controls.control: Other soil amendments (vinasse, cachaza, compost/poultry manure, humus, zeolite, gypsum)
controls.design: field trials reported via CODEX/SENESCYT and Peru studies (secondary; mostly unverifiable)
controls.outcome: Vinasse 1 t/ha: soil Cd 4.87 -> 2.38 mg/kg, bean Cd -45%; cachaza 1 t/ha: bean Cd -44%; compost/poultry manure 30-90 t/ha (Davila 2020, Peru): bean Cd -90% average; compost 1.5-3 t/ha (Florida 2019, CCN-51 Peru): no significant difference; humus 1-2 t/ha: soil Cd -35%; zeolite 2 t/ha: soil Cd -50%; gypsum 1 t/ha: soil -38%, bean -46% (expert considers implausible). Strategy rated Low confidence (31%/19%). Secondary citation reported in the AYS report; Expert Committee could not verify the cited primary in several cases.

controls.control: Low-Cd genotypes, rootstocks, scion grafts, molecular breeding
controls.design: genebank field survey and pot screening (secondary citations)
controls.outcome: Lewis et al. 2018 (Trinidad genebank, 100 genotypes, soil Mehlich-3 Cd 137 ppb, pH 4.96): bean Cd mean 990±43 (SE) ppb, max 2,310 ppb, 13-fold variation among genotypes; leaf Cd 7-fold. Arevalo-Hernandez 2021 (53 genotypes, pot, 28 mg/kg soil Cd): shoot Cd ~0.1-25 mg/kg; CCN-51 2.00 mg/kg. Genetic strategies rated High confidence but long (5-25 years). Secondary citation reported in the AYS report; Expert Committee could not verify the cited primary in several cases.
controls.locator: Attachment 2 s.4.1.5 pp. ~45-47; Attachment 3 s.4.2 p. 34

controls.control: Fermentation management to reduce Cd (acidification, mucilage drainage, microbes)
controls.outcome: Ramtahal 2012: nib and shell Cd increased during fermentation; Vanderschueren 2020: nib Cd decreased (pH <5.0, outward migration to shell); Reyes 2018 mucilage drainage reduced bean Cd (data questioned). No magnitudes given; rated Low confidence (6%).
SD sample sets 'did not reveal a difference between the Cd and Pb levels of alkalyzed and natural products' (no numbers). FDA limit: max 3 parts K2CO3 per 100 parts nibs (21 CFR 163.110).

controls.control: Control of non-cocoa ingredients, packaging, equipment and plant dust
controls.design: SD ingredient testing and site visits
controls.outcome: Dairy ingredients: Cd 60/60 <LOQ; Pb 45/58 <LOQ, 12 at 5.1-12.9 ppb, 1 at 90 ppb. Sugar: Cd 29/30 <LOQ (1 at 363 ppb, a cocoa/sugar blend); Pb 27/30 <LOQ (1 at 50 ppb, blend). Kruszewski 2018: sugar and lecithin <1.3 ppb. Committee concludes processing environment is not a likely Cd/Pb source; shell-in-nib (FDA DAL 1.75%) at 1,000 ppb shell Pb would add 17.5 ppb.

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary lists metals [Pb, Cd] only; the primary also reports aluminium (Al) in Ecuador beans (Tables D-1/D-2) and winnowed nib fractions (Table C-4).

Stored summary does not mention the extensive SD occurrence tables (Root Cause Appendix A Tables 3a-21: >9,000 industry results for beans, powder, liquor, butter, chocolate, nibs and shells by origin/producing country) or the AYS product percentile tables (Attachment 3 Tables 3-6, 10-15), which are the report's main occurrence content.

Stored summary states Chaney Cd feasibility was 'Yes' at the upper level and 'No' at the lower candidate for all three groups; Final Report Table 4 shows Chaney 'Yes' for both 0.960 and 0.800 ppm in Group 3.
Stored summary describes the 0.8 mg Cd/kg value as an EU bean-import limit; the primary only says it is 'usually enforced on bean imports in the EU' (Chaney statement, no legal instrument cited).
Stored summary paraphrases Chaney as 'low nib Pb for beans with as high as 2900 ng Pb/g shell'; primary says 'beans with as high as 2900 ng Pb/g (ppb)' (not shell).

Stored summary sampling_year_range [2014, 2021] - primary data years are 2014-2020 (AYS), 2015-2018 (SD chocolate), 2016-2018 (SD Batch 3), 2019 (Ecuador), 2020 (factory study); 2021 is report drafting, not sampling.
unresolved: SD data are blinded industry results without methods, LOD/LOQ, QA/QC or sampling descriptions; basis (dry vs as-is) and years for Batch 1 beans/powder/liquor/butter and Batch 2 are not reported.
Minimum/maximum/individual SD values were deliberately withheld (confidentiality); only summary statistics are available.
'Peeled cocoa bean' and 'peeled cocoa grains' (Batch 2) are not defined; mapped to form 'nibs' provisionally.
group_kind 'processing_country' is used for 'by Producing Country/Region' tables because the schema enum has no value for country of processing; these must not be read as growing origin.

Exceedance/compliance tables and narrative distribution bands are recorded as statistic 'percentile' with an extra 'exceedance_profile_percent' field or text, because the schema has no exceedance/proportion statistic.

AYS subgroup sample sizes (per cacao group and per organic/single-origin subgroup) are not printed; only overall ~587 products and approximate group shares (40/48/12%). Figure 1-2 bar heights (annual means) are not legible in text extraction.
Table 8 (Attachment 3) and Table 9 headers state 'ppb' while values are clearly ppm/mg/kg; recorded as mg/kg.

Many secondary literature values in Appendix C.2 and Reductions Report were summarised by the Committee without verification (several flagged by the Committee itself as implausible or unverifiable); they should be taken from their own primary sources, not from this report.
Committee-derived Lower/Upper fences (Q1/1.5, Q3x1.5) were not extracted as findings (they are not observed statistics); they remain in reported.text.
Bean Abrasion Study (Attachment 2 Appendix D) reported no metal concentrations (no fine particles released).

FDA Total Diet Study Table 25 (chocolate milk, cake, cookies, candy bars, syrup, pudding) is out of scope for the cocoa page and was not extracted; soil tables 26-27 (US soils, carrots) not extracted.
DiBartolomeis status-quo compliance with his Cd triggers for Group 3 is 42% in Tables 14D/15A but 57% in s.4.3 item 14 and the Final Report summary ('57 to 73%'); unresolved which is correct.
Ramtahal's Pb proposals: Table 3 gives 0.060 (<=65%) and 0.090 (>65-95%), but his text (Attachment 3 p. 28) gives 0.090 for up to 65% and 0.060 for >65-<95%; reversed.
notes: Report-internal secondary citations (Rankin, Manton, Abt, Lo Dico, etc.) are included and flagged in notes as secondary; do not double-count against their own source pages. Units: ppb = µg/kg; ppm = mg/kg (x1000).
